name: Time stretch
threading: Pure functions, safe to call from any non-real-time thread (several at once). Never call from the audio thread.
platforms: Any C++17 compiler. No JUCE, no FFT, no third-party code. Built with floating-point contraction off so the same binary gives identical output.
standalone_test_command: cmake -S modules/time_stretch -B build/time_stretch && cmake --build build/time_stretch && ctest --test-dir build/time_stretch
summary: Offline WSOLA time stretching with chop-anchored regions: each region between anchors is stretched on its own, so every chop boundary lands exactly on its drift-free scaled position and attacks are kept sharp. Three quality presets, progress and cancellation.
public_api: `stretch(input, plan, quality, progress)` returning planar floats of exactly `plan.outFrames` frames
limits: Mono or stereo; tempo change between 0.5x and 2x of the length; regions shorter than three windows are copied (hit mode) instead of stretched
adapters: Run `stretch()` on a worker thread with an immutable copy of the audio; use `mapPosition()` to move markers to the new timeline.
adapter_notes: The caller owns the source rate and the marker list; this module only moves audio and positions.
removal: Delete the folder; callers lose tempo matching only.
